structure: This is one fixed, explicitly assumption-completed association model for the declared peso_lab-weighted complete-case analytical population. Equal-weight rows are independent draws from its joint law, not reconstructed survey records. Age is uniform; recorded female probability increases linearly with age; BMI has an age/sex-dependent mean and bounded, right-skewed beta innovations. Both raw-scale BP conditional means contain age, recorded female, BMI and an age-65 hinge. The hinge permits increasing older-age SBP and decreasing older-age DBP conditional on BMI and sex. INTERSALT coefficients supply BMI slope anchors under an explicit zero-net-adjustment-difference transport assumption. Beijing 65plus raw moments anchor intercepts and a derived innovation covariance after subtracting hypothetical reference predictor covariance. BP innovations follow a bounded bivariate elliptical law. The requested regressions omit the hinge; consequently their residual correlation is not the innovation correlation. No causal interpretation is attached to any coefficient.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Age support, recorded-sex coding, identifier origin and output measurement representation.
parameter_provenance.scale: Raw continuous age and measurements; binary recorded sex; technical integer identifier.
parameter_provenance.unit: Age in baseline years; remaining units follow task columns.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Age bounds and sex coding follow the task. Identifiers start at one. Other continuous variables are generated without rounding or post-generation clipping.
unverified_assumptions: Continuous age is used despite possible integer-year reporting in the release.
No weight/height or final-BP dictionary limits beyond the supplied task schema are available; their reproduction is not claimed.
Bounded model support substitutes for an empirically estimated tail law.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: A=(age-50)/10, B=(BMI-25)/5 and H=max(age-65,0)/10. Female is the task-coded indicator.
parameter_provenance.scale: Centered/scaled design variables and an age hinge.
parameter_provenance.unit: A and H represent ten-year increments; B represents five kg/m^2 increments.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Requested regression centering and scaling are retained. The hinge location is an author assumption aligned with the available older-group boundary, not an estimated biological breakpoint.
unverified_assumptions: A continuous piecewise-linear age mean is adequate across ages 20–79.
The same hinge age applies to both outcomes.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Uniform marginal age distribution and conditional Bernoulli probability P(female=1|age), increasing from 0.48 to 0.56 across the age support.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Age is marginal; recorded sex is conditional on age.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Author-selected composition, not estimated from any supplied source or target records.
unverified_assumptions: This composition represents the weighted selected population.
Age and sex are dependent through the specified probability function.
Source age/sex proportions are not used as estimates of target composition.

parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Baseline age and recorded female indicator.
parameter_provenance.unit: Intercept and female shift in kg/m^2; age coefficient in kg/m^2 per ten years.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Explicit completion of unidentified target BMI composition and dependence.
unverified_assumptions: No nonlinear age term or age-by-sex interaction in the BMI mean.
The same conditional mean is used as a hypothetical BMI bridge for Beijing calibration.
These numbers are not inferred from INTERSALT illustrative centre means.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: BMI innovation equals 4.8 times a mean-centered, unit-SD Beta(2,5) variable.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Conditional on age and recorded sex, with a common innovation distribution.
parameter_provenance.scale: Individual conditional dispersion and bounded skewed distribution.
parameter_provenance.unit: Innovation SD is kg/m^2; beta shapes are dimensionless.
parameter_provenance.derivation: For shapes alpha and beta, the program uses mean alpha/(alpha+beta) and variance alpha*beta/((alpha+beta)^2*(alpha+beta+1)) before rescaling.
unverified_assumptions: BMI innovations are independent of age and sex and have constant variance.
The positive skew and finite tails are scenario choices.
The 4.8 SD is not a source SE and is not obtained by pooling INTERSALT averaged subgroup SDs.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: SBP/DBP conditional-mean coefficient vectors: age [5,1.5], female [-4,-2], and age-65 hinge [3,-5], in outcome order.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Age, female, BMI and age hinge jointly.
parameter_provenance.scale: Raw-scale arithmetic conditional means, not causal effects.
parameter_provenance.unit: Age and hinge coefficients in mmHg per ten-year basis unit; female coefficients in mmHg.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Author-selected age and sex association scenario. Above age 65, age slopes at fixed BMI and sex are the sums of age and hinge coefficients.
unverified_assumptions: No BMI-by-age or BMI-by-sex interaction.
No additional nonlinear BMI effect.
Age and sex coefficients are not estimated by contrasting Beijing group means.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Reported inverse-variance-pooled within-centre raw BP-on-BMI regression coefficients and their coefficient SEs; subsequently rescaled and assumed to be target conditional-mean slopes.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Source: age, sex, urinary sodium, urinary potassium, alcohol 1–299 ml/week indicator and alcohol at least 300 ml/week indicator. Generated law: age, female, BMI and age hinge.
parameter_provenance.scale: Reported raw linear regression slopes and coefficient sampling uncertainty.
parameter_provenance.unit: Reported slopes and SEs in mmHg per kg/m^2; generated BMI coefficients in mmHg per five kg/m^2.

source_pointers.population: 10,079 adults aged 20–59 in 52 centres across 32 countries; antihypertensive treatment not excluded
source_pointers.measurement: Mean of two seated Hawksley random-zero readings after five-minute rest; height and weight measured twice

parameter_provenance.derivation: Multiply each reported slope by the specified BMI scale. SEs remain metadata and are never used as person-level noise. The slope transfer is an assumption, not evidence of estimand equivalence.
unverified_assumptions: The net change in BMI slope from removing urinary sodium, potassium and alcohol adjustment is exactly zero. This asserts a zero net projection contribution, not independence of those omitted variables.
Within-centre pooled slopes transfer without centre-selection or aggregation bias to the defined target mixture.
Slopes extrapolate unchanged through ages 60–79 and across source/target measurement protocols.
Treatment and other omitted factors are implicitly marginalized without changing these conditional slopes.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Unadjusted older-group counts, arithmetic means and individual SDs used as rounded calibration anchors.
parameter_provenance.scale: Raw moments; SDs describe individuals, not coefficient uncertainty.
parameter_provenance.unit: Age in years; BP and pulse pressure in mmHg; counts in persons.

source_pointers.population: 2009 selected Beijing middle-aged/older community participants; prior MI/stroke/severe CHF, blood-sample refusal and missingness excluded; antihypertensive use retained
source_pointers.measurement: Omron HEM-4021 seated non-dominant-arm BP after five-minute rest; average of two readings within two minutes

parameter_provenance.derivation: Reference female probability is 1-male_n/n. Only the 65plus row is used for calibration.
unverified_assumptions: Rounded published moments are treated as exact scenario anchors.
The selected source group's mean levels and covariance can anchor the target after the specified covariate bridge.
The full source age range was not verified; source reference moments are not constrained to target age support.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Hypothetical reference covariate moments required to remove explained covariance: zero age–female covariance, generated BMI conditional moments, and a linear active hinge throughout the older group.
parameter_provenance.scale: Raw covariance and conditional moment bridge.
parameter_provenance.unit: Age–female covariance in years times the binary indicator; BMI moments in kg/m^2 and squared kg/m^2.

source_pointers.locator: Table 1, 65plus group definition; BMI_reported=false in supplied packet

parameter_provenance.derivation: The source reports no BMI moments or age–sex covariance. Their values are completed explicitly rather than inferred from the absence of reporting.
unverified_assumptions: Age and female have zero covariance in the source calibration group, although they are dependent in the target model.
The target BMI conditional mean and innovation variance also apply to this hypothetical older reference population.
BMI innovations have zero covariance with source age and sex.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Derived BP intercept vector and conditional innovation covariance matrix.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: Calibration removes the covariance of conditional means given source age, female and BMI; the resulting covariance is then used conditional on target covariates.
parameter_provenance.scale: Raw conditional means and covariances, distinct from source marginal moments.
parameter_provenance.unit: Intercepts in mmHg; covariance entries in mmHg^2.

source_pointers.locator: Table 1, 65plus SBP, DBP and pulse-pressure SDs

parameter_provenance.derivation: Let b be the rescaled BMI coefficient vector, a/f/h the age/female/hinge vectors, u/v the BMI age/female coefficients, s the BMI scale, and p the reference female probability. Above the hinge, q_A=a+h*age_scale/hinge_scale+b*u/s and q_F=f+b*v/s. The explained covariance is outer(q_A,q_A)*Var(A)+outer(q_F,q_F)*p*(1-p)+outer(b,b)*(BMI_innovation_SD/s)^2 plus the specified age–female cross term. Subtract it from the raw BP covariance recovered using pulse pressure. Intercepts are source BP means minus mean predictor contributions.
unverified_assumptions: Pulse pressure equals SBP minus DBP on the same paired readings and analysis sample.
The raw covariance identity is exact apart from source rounding; it does not identify a residual correlation by itself.
The assumed reference predictor contribution, rather than evidence alone, determines the subtraction.
The generated constant innovation covariance and mean calibration transport across populations and protocols.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Independent-of-covariates BP innovation vector obtained by applying the derived covariance Cholesky factor to a uniform disk of radius two.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: All generated age, sex and BMI values.
parameter_provenance.scale: Bounded elliptical individual residual distribution with zero mean and constant covariance.
parameter_provenance.unit: Standardized radius dimensionless; transformed innovations in mmHg.
parameter_provenance.derivation: A uniform two-dimensional disk of radius two has identity covariance. Multiplication by the Cholesky factor therefore gives the calibrated innovation covariance without clipping.
unverified_assumptions: Ellipse shape, bounded tails, homoscedasticity and covariate independence are author assumptions.
SBP and DBP innovations are jointly dependent; even their whitened disk coordinates are not independent.
There are no additional treatment, disease, measurement-error or outlier mixtures.
The innovation correlation is not equated to the requested regression-residual correlation.

parameter_provenance.meaning_statistical_operator: Fixed-parameter scenario with individual sampling variation but no parameter or transport uncertainty draws.
parameter_provenance.conditioning_set: All supplied anchors and author assumptions held fixed.
parameter_provenance.scale: Separation of individual variability, source sampling uncertainty and unidentified transport uncertainty.
parameter_provenance.derivation: Source slope SEs are retained but not sampled. No coefficient covariance, source-moment sampling model or quantitative transfer uncertainty is supplied. Rounding envelopes are not treated as confidence intervals.
unverified_assumptions: A single fixed scenario is sufficient for this deliverable, not for uncertainty-aware substantive inference.
Changing the seed samples persons from the same law and does not explore model uncertainty.

requested_estimands.derivation_or_reason: This is a derived projection value, not merely a copied source coefficient. In the generated law, residualizing B on intercept, A and female leaves only the independent centered BMI innovation divided by five. This residual is orthogonal to the age hinge and BP innovations. Frisch–Waugh–Lovell therefore gives the population coefficient of B as the conditional BMI coefficient, 5*0.7754, despite omission of the hinge from the requested regression. This equality relies on the stated BMI dependence and slope-transfer assumptions.

Residualized B is independent of the age hinge and orthogonal to the DBP innovation under this law. Thus the population OLS coefficient on B is 5*0.5967 by Frisch–Waugh–Lovell. The source adjustment set alone does not establish this equality; the explicit transport and BMI-composition assumptions do.
A numerical population correlation has not been evaluated. Its analytic characterization is given below; neither a finite-sample correlation nor the Beijing raw correlation is substituted.
requested_estimands.population_formula: Let Sigma be the innovation covariance computed by the declared calibration. Let V=14^3*45^3/(3*59^4*10^2), the variance of the age-65 hinge after linear projection on intercept and age under Uniform(20,79). Because E(female|age) is affine and BMI equals an affine age/sex mean plus independent noise, adding female and BMI to that hinge projection changes no coefficients. The requested paired residuals are therefore R_S=e_S+3*H_res and R_D=e_D-5*H_res. Their population Pearson correlation is (Sigma_SD-15*V)/sqrt((Sigma_SS+9*V)*(Sigma_DD+25*V)).

limitations: No target records, weights or target outcome summaries were used. The generated law is asserted to represent the declared weighted analytical distribution only through explicit transport assumptions; national representativeness is not asserted.

Age/sex/BMI composition, their dependencies, conditional age/sex effects, tails and transfer uncertainty remain unidentified by the supplied evidence. The construction selects one usable scenario rather than estimating those relationships.

The population definition already conditions on admissible baseline measurements, laboratory weight, complete cases and pregnancy exclusion. These selection events are not simulated. Unknown/inapplicable pregnancy is implicitly retained; no HbA1c, treatment or hypertension restriction is imposed.

Baseline BP timing is retained conceptually. The released final-reading aggregation is unknown. Transport from two-reading source averages to that measurement is assumed without a separate measurement-error model.
No explicit weight, height, pregnancy, medication, centre, disease, urinary-electrolyte or alcohol variables are generated. Their marginalization and selection effects are not empirically identified.

The older Beijing calibration population differs materially from the target and includes source-specific exclusions. Its unknown BMI distribution is replaced with an assumed bridge. The source's raw covariance does not authenticate the resulting conditional covariance.
Only Beijing 65plus summaries are used. Overall and under65 summaries are dependent evidence from the same cohort and are not treated as replications or additional calibration targets.

INTERSALT illustrative centre SDs are averages of subgroup SDs, not pooled population SDs; none are used to set individual dispersion. INTERMAP contributes no admitted numerical BP/BMI calibration and is deliberately unused.

Bounded beta and elliptical tails suppress sufficiently extreme observations and do not represent empirically verified obesity, hypertension or hypotension tails. No post-generation clipping is used because it would change the declared projections.
The source coefficient SEs do not quantify transport uncertainty. No uncertainty intervals for the target estimands are supplied by this fixed scenario.
Curator statements about original scans and tables are historical provenance. The supplied sources and extraction artifacts have not been freshly authenticated.

The Python module and its numerical covariance construction have not been executed or software-tested here. Scientific identification and transport validity would not follow from successful execution.
